NICE Guideline CG150: Headaches in Over 12s Diagnosis and Management | Publisher: National
Headache Red Flags Requiring Immediate Emergency Referral
Urgent Red Flags (SNOOP Criteria): - Sudden onset severe headache reaching
peak intensity within seconds ('thunderclap' headache). - Headache
accompanied by fever, stiff neck, confusion, seizure, or focal
neurological deficits (weakness, numbness, vision loss). - New headache in
patients with history of cancer or immunocompromise. - Headache associated
with recent head trauma or worsening with coughing/straining. -
Progressive headache worsening over days or weeks in adults over 50.
